raw_case_text:
A 78-year-old gentleman, who was a farmer by occupation, currently retired, hailing from Tamil Nadu, presented with a 6-month history of a swelling over the right side of the neck. The swelling was gradual in onset, progressive in its size over the course of 6 months. The patient also developed dull aching pain over the swelling for the past 2 months. There were no radiation of the pain, associated weakness of the extremities, or any sensory deficits. There was no history of trauma in the recent past or any other constitutional symptoms. The patient is not a diabetic. He is a K/c/o hypertension, COPD, and BPH for which he has been on treatment. On examination, there was a globular swelling of size 10 x 8 cm which was palpable over the right shoulder. The mass was seen extending superiorly, 8 cm below the mastoid tip to until the spine of scapula, mediolaterally from the midline, up to the medial border of scapula. On palpation, there was no local warmth or tenderness, globular swelling was felt which was firm in consistency with well-defined margins. The skin over the swelling was pinchable. The swelling was mobile in the coronal plane. There was no associated weakness or sensory deficits in the right upper limb. Movements of the shoulder were also unaffected.
X-rays of the neck were suggestive of a soft-tissue mass in the inferior aspect of the neck with multiple ovoid calcifications (Fig. 1 and 2). Fine-needle aspiration cytology was done, which was inconclusive. The patient was further planned for magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the neck, which showed an ill-defined, lobulated lesion measuring 4.0 x 7.0 x 5.4 cm, in the right trapezius muscle at C6-T2 level (Fig. 3). The lesion was isointense in T1 images with mild diffusion restriction, showing multiple ovoid lesions (Fig. 4) and heterogeneous in T2 images (Fig. 5), short tau inversion recovery images (Fig. 6, 7 and 8). The lesion was also hypovascular on screening Doppler. There were no hemorrhagic spots and calcifications noted in the collection (Fig. 5). MRI again was reported with a differential of neurocysticercosis or fibromatosis.
Neurocysticercosis.
Fibromatosis.
Open biopsy was done which showed benign spindle cell lesion infiltrating skeletal muscles, focal reactive skeletal bundle, with no necrosis, and no increase in mitosis. The tumor cells were positive for vimentin, focally positive for beta-catenin, and smooth muscle actin (SMA) (Fig. 9 and 10). The cells were negative for S100. Hence, the lesion was suggestive of fibromatosis.
The patient was planned for wide local excision. A horizontal incision was made over the tumor and the overlying muscles were separated. The entire tumor was removed in toto (Fig. 11 and 12) which measured 9.0 x 8.5 x 6.0 cm. The cut surface showed an ill-defined gray-white lesion which was hard in consistency and the margins were reported to be free off the tumor. The post-operative period was uneventful and recovered completely. Power of the right upper limb and, movements of the shoulder are unaffected. The patient was started postoperatively on nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for a period of 1 month. The patient was not willing for radiotherapy and hence was deferred. He has been on regular follow-up for the past 2 years. There is no evidence of residual disease or recurrence of the tumor (Fig. 13 and 14).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 78-year-old retired male farmer from Tamil Nadu presented with a 6-month history of a progressively enlarging right neck and shoulder swelling and a 2-month history of dull aching pain over the mass.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient noticed a gradually enlarging swelling over the right side of his neck and shoulder 6 months prior to presentation, which became associated with a dull, non-radiating ache over the preceding 2 months. There was no extremity weakness, sensory loss, recent trauma, or constitutional symptoms.
subjective.past_medical_history: Retired farmer from Tamil Nadu with a known history of hypertension, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) on medical therapy; non-diabetic and no history of recent trauma.
subjective.review_of_systems: Negative for radiating pain, upper limb weakness or numbness, fever, weight loss, or other constitutional symptoms; on regular medications for hypertension, COPD, and BPH.

objective.physical_examination: Local examination revealed a firm, well-defined, non-tender, non-warm 10 x 8 cm globular mass over the right shoulder and inferior neck (extending from 8 cm below the mastoid tip to the spine of the scapula and from the midline to the medial scapular border), mobile in the coronal plane with pinchable overlying skin. Right shoulder range of motion and right upper extremity motor and sensory examinations were completely normal.
objective.routine_investigations: Neck radiographs showed a soft-tissue mass in the inferior neck with multiple ovoid calcifications. Screening Doppler ultrasound showed the lesion was hypovascular. Fine-needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) was inconclusive.
objective.advanced_workup: Neck MRI revealed an ill-defined lobulated lesion measuring 4.0 x 7.0 x 5.4 cm within the right trapezius muscle at the C6-T2 level, appearing T1-isointense with mild diffusion restriction and multiple ovoid internal foci and heterogeneous on T2 and STIR sequences without hemorrhage or calcification inside the collection. Open incisional biopsy demonstrated a benign spindle cell lesion infiltrating skeletal muscle fibers without necrosis or increased mitotic activity; immunohistochemistry was positive for vimentin, focally positive for beta-catenin and smooth muscle actin (SMA), and negative for S100.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Open biopsy histopathology and immunohistochemistry (vimentin+, beta-catenin+, SMA+, S100-) confirmed intramuscular desmoid-type fibromatosis of the right trapezius muscle, ruling out the radiological differential diagnosis of myocysticercosis/neurocysticercosis. He underwent complete wide local excision of the 9.0 x 8.5 x 6.0 cm hard gray-white tumor with tumor-free margins and received a 1-month postoperative course of NSAIDs (declining adjuvant radiotherapy). He recovered with full right shoulder and arm function and had no recurrence over 2 years of follow-up.
